title: Best Album Cover Designers (2026): How to Hire One
description: How to hire an album or single cover designer: what the package should include, streaming sizes, rights, price factors and red flags.
intro: Your cover art is the first thing listeners see on streaming platforms, usually as a tiny square. It needs to reflect the music, stay readable at small sizes and meet each platform's rules. Covers get rejected or cause problems when they use images without rights, include forbidden elements, or are delivered in the wrong size. This guide helps you get cover art ready for release.

faq.q: What size should cover art be?
faq.a: Most distributors ask for a square image at high resolution, typically at least 3000 by 3000 pixels, in JPG or PNG. Check your distributor's current requirements before ordering.

faq.q: What can get cover art rejected?
faq.a: Common reasons include blurry images, website addresses or social handles, logos of stores or brands, misleading text and explicit content that is not labeled. Read your distributor's artwork rules.

faq.q: Can the designer use photos from the internet?
faq.a: Only licensed images or photos you own. Using images without permission can get your release taken down.

faq.q: Do I need versions for social media?
faq.a: It helps. Ask for vertical versions for stories and a banner for your profiles, in the same style.
Confirm in writing that you may use the art for the release, merchandise and promotion.
